prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: For the past three consecutive months, (A) / the research team is working tirelessly (B) / on developing a stable synthetic vaccine strain. (C) / No Error (D)
options: For the past three consecutive months, (A)
the research team is working tirelessly (B)
on developing a stable synthetic vaccine strain. (C)
explanation: An action continuing over a stated past period ('for the past three months') requires the present perfect continuous: 'has been working tirelessly'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The young child has been crying (A) / continuously for the past one hour (B) / because he had lost his favorite toy. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The young child has been crying
continuously for the past one hour
because he had lost his favorite toy.
explanation: The cause is still relevant to the present continuing action, so the present perfect is needed: 'because he has lost his favorite toy'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My father did not yet receive (A) / the formal retirement pension orders (B) / from the central administrative cell. (C) / No Error (D)
options: My father did not yet receive
explanation: The adverb 'yet' in a negative sentence about a still-pending action requires the present perfect: 'has not yet received'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It is he who work for the company for more than a decade.
explanation: 'for more than a decade' signals present perfect and the verb must agree with 'he', so 'who has worked' is correct.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My brother lost / his job during the lockdown, / but he had got / a new job now.
explanation: 'Now' signals present perfect, so 'he had got' should be 'he has got'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: How long are you working / for your current employer / and why don’t you / look for better opportunities?
explanation: 'How long' with an action continuing up to now requires the present perfect continuous: 'How long have you been working'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This is the first time / I ate such / a tasty cake.
explanation: After 'This is the first time', the present perfect is required: 'I have eaten such a tasty cake.'

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. One of them contains an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options.
sentence: She has been speaking / to him on / the subject / many times.
explanation: 'Many times' denotes a completed, repeated action, so the present perfect 'has spoken' is required instead of the present perfect continuous.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. How long you are living in this city?
explanation: 'How long' with a state continuing to the present takes the present perfect with inverted question order: 'have you lived'.

explanation: The present perfect 'have arrived' links the completed arrival with the present situation of the guests sitting in the garden.
